content.english: Ant. Alleluia, * make thy face to shine upon thy servant, alleluia, alleluia.

content.latin: 118:129 (Phe) Mirabília testimónia tua: * ídeo scrutáta est ea ánima mea.
content.english: 118:129 (Phe) Thy testimonies are wonderful: * therefore my soul hath sought them.

content.latin: 118:130 Declarátio sermónum tuórum illúminat: * et intelléctum dat párvulis.
content.english: 118:130 The declaration of thy words giveth light: * and giveth understanding to little ones.

content.latin: 118:131 Os meum apérui, et attráxi spíritum: * quia mandáta tua desiderábam.
content.english: 118:131 I opened my mouth, and panted: * because I longed for thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:132 Áspice in me, et miserére mei, * secúndum iudícium diligéntium nomen tuum.
content.english: 118:132 Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me, * according to the judgment of them that love thy name.

content.latin: 118:133 Gressus meos dírige secúndum elóquium tuum: * et non dominétur mei omnis iniustítia.
content.english: 118:133 Direct my steps according to thy word: * and let no iniquity have dominion over me.

content.latin: 118:134 Rédime me a calúmniis hóminum: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:134 Redeem me from the calumnies of men: * that I may keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:135 Fáciem tuam illúmina super servum tuum: * et doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:135 Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: * and teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:136 Éxitus aquárum deduxérunt óculi mei: * quia non custodiérunt legem tuam.
content.english: 118:136 My eyes have sent forth springs of water: * because they have not kept thy law.

content.latin: 118:137 (Sade) Iustus es, Dómine: * et rectum iudícium tuum.
content.english: 118:137 (Sade) Thou art just, O Lord: * and thy judgment is right.

content.latin: 118:138 Mandásti iustítiam testimónia tua: * et veritátem tuam nimis.
content.english: 118:138 Thou hast commanded justice thy testimonies: * and thy truth exceedingly.

content.latin: 118:139 Tabéscere me fecit zelus meus: * quia oblíti sunt verba tua inimíci mei.
content.english: 118:139 My zeal hath made me pine away: * because my enemies forgot thy words.

content.latin: 118:140 Ignítum elóquium tuum veheménter: * et servus tuus diléxit illud.
content.english: 118:140 Thy word is exceedingly refined: * and thy servant hath loved it.

content.latin: 118:141 Adolescéntulus sum ego et contémptus: * iustificatiónes tuas non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:141 I am very young and despised; but * I forget not thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:142 Iustítia tua, iustítia in ætérnum: * et lex tua véritas.
content.english: 118:142 Thy justice is justice for ever: * and thy law is the truth.

content.latin: 118:143 Tribulátio, et angústia invenérunt me: * mandáta tua meditátio mea est.
content.english: 118:143 Trouble and anguish have found me: * thy commandments are my meditation.

content.latin: 118:144 Ǽquitas testimónia tua in ætérnum: * intelléctum da mihi, et vivam.
content.english: 118:144 Thy testimonies are justice for ever: * give me understanding, and I shall live.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:145 (Coph) Clamávi in toto corde meo, exáudi me, Dómine: * iustificatiónes tuas requíram.
content.english: 118:145 (Coph) I cried with my whole heart, hear me, O Lord: * I will seek thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:146 Clamávi ad te, salvum me fac: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:146 I cried unto thee, save me: * that I may keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:147 Prævéni in maturitáte, et clamávi: * quia in verba tua supersperávi.
content.english: 118:147 I prevented the dawning of the day, and cried: * because in thy words I very much hoped.

content.latin: 118:148 Prævenérunt óculi mei ad te dilúculo: * ut meditárer elóquia tua.
content.english: 118:148 My eyes to thee have prevented the morning: * that I might meditate on thy words.

content.latin: 118:149 Vocem meam audi secúndum misericórdiam tuam, Dómine: * et secúndum iudícium tuum vivífica me.
content.english: 118:149 Hear thou my voice, O Lord, according to thy mercy: * and quicken me according to thy judgment.

content.latin: 118:150 Appropinquavérunt persequéntes me iniquitáti: * a lege autem tua longe facti sunt.
content.english: 118:150 They that persecute me have drawn nigh to iniquity; * but they are gone far off from thy law.

content.latin: 118:151 Prope es tu, Dómine: * et omnes viæ tuæ véritas.
content.english: 118:151 Thou art near, O Lord: * and all thy ways are truth.

content.latin: 118:152 Inítio cognóvi de testimóniis tuis: * quia in ætérnum fundásti ea.
content.english: 118:152 I have known from the beginning concerning thy testimonies: * that thou hast founded them for ever.

content.latin: 118:153 (Res) Vide humilitátem meam, et éripe me: * quia legem tuam non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:153 (Res) See my humiliation and deliver me: * for I have not forgotten thy law.

content.latin: 118:154 Iúdica iudícium meum, et rédime me: * propter elóquium tuum vivífica me.
content.english: 118:154 Judge my judgment and redeem me: * quicken thou me for thy word’s sake.

content.latin: 118:155 Longe a peccatóribus salus: * quia iustificatiónes tuas non exquisiérunt.
content.english: 118:155 Salvation is far from sinners; * because they have not sought thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:156 Misericórdiæ tuæ multæ, Dómine: * secúndum iudícium tuum vivífica me.
content.english: 118:156 Many, O Lord, are thy mercies: * quicken me according to thy judgment.

content.latin: 118:157 Multi qui persequúntur me, et tríbulant me: * a testimóniis tuis non declinávi.
content.english: 118:157 Many are they that persecute me, and afflict me; * but I have not declined from thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:158 Vidi prævaricántes, et tabescébam: * quia elóquia tua non custodiérunt.
content.english: 118:158 I beheld the transgressors, and I pined away; * because they kept not thy word.

content.latin: 118:159 Vide quóniam mandáta tua diléxi, Dómine: * in misericórdia tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:159 Behold I have loved thy commandments, O Lord; * quicken me thou in thy mercy.

content.latin: 118:160 Princípium verbórum tuórum, véritas: * in ætérnum ómnia iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:160 The beginning of thy words is truth: * all the judgments of thy justice are for ever.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:161 (Sin) Príncipes persecúti sunt me gratis: * et a verbis tuis formidávit cor meum.
content.english: 118:161 (Sin) Princes have persecuted me without cause: * and my heart hath been in awe of thy words.

content.latin: 118:162 Lætábor ego super elóquia tua: * sicut qui invénit spólia multa.
content.english: 118:162 I will rejoice at thy words, * as one that hath found great spoil.

content.latin: 118:163 Iniquitátem ódio hábui, et abominátus sum: * legem autem tuam diléxi.
content.english: 118:163 I have hated and abhorred iniquity; * but I have loved thy law.

content.latin: 118:164 Sépties in die laudem dixi tibi, * super iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:164 Seven times a day I have given praise to thee, * for the judgments of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:165 Pax multa diligéntibus legem tuam: * et non est illis scándalum.
content.english: 118:165 Much peace have they that love thy law, * and to them there is no stumbling-block.

content.latin: 118:166 Exspectábam salutáre tuum, Dómine: * et mandáta tua diléxi.
content.english: 118:166 I looked for thy salvation, O Lord: * and I loved thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:167 Custodívit ánima mea testimónia tua: * et diléxit ea veheménter.
content.english: 118:167 My soul hath kept thy testimonies: * and hath loved them exceedingly.

content.latin: 118:168 Servávi mandáta tua, et testimónia tua: * quia omnes viæ meæ in conspéctu tuo.
content.english: 118:168 I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies: * because all my ways are in thy sight.

content.latin: 118:169 (Thau) Appropínquet deprecátio mea in conspéctu tuo, Dómine: * iuxta elóquium tuum da mihi intelléctum.
content.english: 118:169 (Tau) Let my supplication, O Lord, come near in thy sight: * give me understanding according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:170 Intret postulátio mea in conspéctu tuo: * secúndum elóquium tuum éripe me.
content.english: 118:170 Let my request come in before thee; * deliver thou me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:171 Eructábunt lábia mea hymnum, * cum docúeris me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:171 My lips shall utter a hymn, * when thou shalt teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:172 Pronuntiábit lingua mea elóquium tuum: * quia ómnia mandáta tua ǽquitas.
content.english: 118:172 My tongue shall pronounce thy word: * because all thy commandments are justice.

content.latin: 118:173 Fiat manus tua ut salvet me: * quóniam mandáta tua elégi.
content.english: 118:173 Let thy hand be with me to save me; * for I have chosen thy precepts.

content.latin: 118:174 Concupívi salutáre tuum, Dómine: * et lex tua meditátio mea est.
content.english: 118:174 I have longed for thy salvation, O Lord; * and thy law is my meditation.

content.latin: 118:175 Vivet ánima mea, et laudábit te: * et iudícia tua adiuvábunt me.
content.english: 118:175 My soul shall live and shall praise thee: * and thy judgments shall help me.

content.latin: 118:176 Errávi, sicut ovis, quæ périit: * quære servum tuum, quia mandáta tua non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:176 I have gone astray like a sheep that is lost: * seek thy servant, because I have not forgotten thy commandments.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Allelúia, fáciem tuam, Dómine, illúmina super servum tuum, allelúia, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Alleluia, make thy face to shine upon thy servant, alleluia, alleluia.

content.latin: Empti enim estis prétio magno. Glorificáte et portáte Deum in córpore vestro.
content.english: For you are bought with a great price. Glorify and bear God in your body.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℟.br. I cried with my whole heart, * hear me, O Lord.

content.english: ℟. I cried with my whole heart, * hear me, O Lord.

content.english: ℣. From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: ℟. And from those of others spare thy servant.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui diligéntibus te bona invisibília præparásti: infúnde córdibus nostris tui amóris afféctum; ut te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, promissiónes tuas, quæ omne desidérium súperant, consequámur.
content.english: O God, Who hast prepared for them that love thee such good things as pass man's understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward thee, that we, loving thee in all things and above all things, may obtain thy promises, which exceed all that we can desire.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Ant. Peter and John * went up together into the Temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.

content.latin: Psalmus 109 [1]
content.english: Psalm 109 [1]

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Peter and John went up together into the Temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.

content.english: Ant. Silver and gold have I none, * but such as I have, give I thee.

content.latin: Psalmus 110 [2]
content.english: Psalm 110 [2]

content.latin: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.
content.english: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

content.latin: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.
content.english: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

content.latin: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

content.latin: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.
content.english: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: * he hath given food to them that fear him.

content.latin: 110:5 Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
content.english: 110:5 He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

content.latin: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.
content.english: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

content.latin: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
content.english: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

content.latin: 110:9 Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
content.english: 110:9 He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

content.latin: 110:9 (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
content.english: 110:9 (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

content.latin: 110:10 Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:10 A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. The Angel said unto Peter: * Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

content.latin: Psalmus 111 [3]
content.english: Psalm 111 [3]

content.latin: 111:1 Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.
content.english: 111:1 Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.

content.latin: 111:2 Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
content.english: 111:2 His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

content.latin: 111:3 Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 111:3 Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

content.latin: 111:4 Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.
content.english: 111:4 To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.

content.latin: 111:5 Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
content.english: 111:5 Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: he shall order his words with judgment: * because he shall not be moved for ever.

content.latin: 111:7 In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
content.english: 111:7 The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.

content.latin: 111:7 Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
content.english: 111:7 His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.

content.latin: 111:9 Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.
content.english: 111:9 He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.

content.latin: 111:10 Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
content.english: 111:10 The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.

content.english: Ant. The Angel said unto Peter: Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

content.english: Ant. The Lord hath sent * His Angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, alleluia.

content.latin: Psalmus 112 [4]
content.english: Psalm 112 [4]

content.latin: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
content.english: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

content.latin: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

content.latin: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.
content.english: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

content.latin: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
content.english: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

content.latin: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
content.english: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

content.latin: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
content.english: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

content.latin: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
content.english: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

content.latin: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
content.english: 90:1 He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, * shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 90:2 Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
content.english: 90:2 He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: * my God, in him will I trust.

content.latin: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
content.english: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

content.latin: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
content.english: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

content.latin: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
content.english: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

content.latin: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.
content.english: 90:6 Of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the business that walketh about in the dark: * of invasion, or of the noonday devil.

content.latin: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
content.english: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

content.latin: 90:8 Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
content.english: 90:8 But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: * and shalt see the reward of the wicked.

content.latin: 90:9 Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
content.english: 90:9 Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: * thou hast made the most High thy refuge.

content.latin: 90:10 Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
content.english: 90:10 There shall no evil come to thee: * nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.

content.latin: 90:11 Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
content.english: 90:11 For he hath given his angels charge over thee; * to keep thee in all thy ways.

content.latin: 90:12 In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
content.english: 90:12 In their hands they shall bear thee up: * lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

content.latin: 90:13 Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
content.english: 90:13 Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.

content.latin: 90:14 Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
content.english: 90:14 Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he hath known my name.

content.latin: 90:15 Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
content.english: 90:15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: * I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.

content.latin: 90:16 Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.

content.english: O Father, that we ask be done,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Jer 14:9

content.latin: Tu autem in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos, Dómine, Deus noster.
content.english: But thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy name is called upon by us: forsake us not, O Lord our God.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟.br. In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟.br. Into thy hands, O Lord, * do I commend my spirit.

content.english: ℟. Into thy hands, O Lord, * do I commend my spirit.

content.latin: ℣. Redemísti nos, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
content.english: ℣. For thou hast redeemed us, O Lord, God of truth.

content.latin: ℟. Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟. I commend my spirit.

content.latin: ℟. In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟. Into thy hands, O Lord, * do I commend my spirit.

content.latin: ℣. Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.
content.english: ℣. Keep us, Lord, as the apple of thine eye.

content.latin: ℟. Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
content.english: ℟. Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, * Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, * Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

content.latin: 2:29 Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:
content.english: 2:29 Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, ✠ * according to thy word in peace;

content.latin: 2:30 Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
content.english: 2:30 Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,

content.latin: 2:31 Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,
content.english: 2:31 Which thou hast prepared * before the face of all peoples:

content.latin: 2:32 Lumen ad revelatiónem géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.
content.english: 2:32 A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, * and the glory of thy people Israel.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.
